sentences.text: The assessment was conducted by Social Worker Priya Nair with Margaret Doyle and her son Kevin Doyle present.

Margaret Doyle lives in a house with her cat, Biscuit, and has a history of three falls in the last six months, including a significant fall on March 3rd where she was on the floor for approximately two hours.
The assessment is taking place following a referral from the hospital after Margaret's discharge.
The purpose of the visit is to conduct a needs assessment under the Care Act to understand how Margaret is managing day-to-day and identify potential support.
Margaret explicitly stated she did not want to be put anywhere, clarifying that the assessment is about supporting her in her own home.
Margaret uses a walking frame indoors most of the time and a stick outdoors, though she sometimes holds onto furniture instead of using the frame.
She has been unable to walk to the shops since the fall, expressing fear of going out again.
Margaret has had three falls in the last six months: one in the garden before Christmas, one in the bathroom in January, and the significant fall on March 3rd.
She did not tell her GP about the two earlier falls, though her son Kevin knows about the garden fall.
Her left wrist was fractured; she has since had the cast removed and is now wearing a splint, which she finds difficult to manage.
Getting dressed takes between 40 minutes and an hour, often requiring her to sit down in between, and she has given up wearing tights.
Margaret has not had a proper bath since January due to fear of getting stuck and not being able to get out with her injured wrist.
She washes herself at the sink using a flannel and relies on Brenda next door to wash her hair occasionally.
She has not cooked since the fall because she cannot lift the pans and feels frightened of the kitchen.
Her diet is limited to toast, soup, and occasionally a yoghurt or crackers; she has lost nearly a stone since Christmas.
Margaret stated she wants to stay in her own home for as long as possible, valuing her garden, her cat, and her neighbours.
She expressed a strong preference to remain in her current house rather than moving to a sheltered flat or bungalow, citing her attachment to the property and her late husband Frank.
She would prefer to be cared for at Beechwood if she ever needed to move, as she had positive experiences there.
Margaret wants to be able to cook a proper dinner occasionally and to return to the lunch club at St Michael's church.
She expressed a desire to be able to have a proper bath and wash her hair again.
She is concerned about being frightened constantly and wants to feel safe in her kitchen.
Margaret stated she does not want the police involved in the matter regarding her grandson's use of her bank card.
She wants her grandson to stop using her card and for it to be returned to her.
She expressed a wish to be able to cook herself a proper dinner again, not every day but now and then.
She wants to be able to see her roses bloom this summer and go out to look at them.
Margaret disclosed that her grandson, Jordan, has been borrowing her bank card to get cash or shop for himself.
She revealed that her bank statements showed approximately six hundred pounds in withdrawals over the last two months that she did not authorize.
She confirmed she gave her grandson her bank card number and PIN when she was discharged from the hospital so he could do her shopping.
Her son Kevin reported that Brenda next door saw Jordan at a cash machine with a card, though Kevin noted Brenda was not sure it was Jordan.
Kevin mentioned hearing from one of Jordan's old mates' mothers that Jordan has gotten into debt with betting apps on his phone.
The social worker recorded Kevin's report about the betting debt as second-hand information, noting it was not confirmed as fact.
Margaret denied having any thoughts of harming herself or ending her life, stating she has too much to live for.
She disclosed that she has missed her blood pressure tablets twice in the last week.
Margaret reported occasional incontinence, sometimes leaking if she holds it too long, and currently wears pads at night.
She described feeling lonely on days when no one visits, noting she sometimes does not get dressed and stays in her nightie.
Margaret's son Kevin visits mainly on Sundays to do the big shop and sit with her, sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts.
Her daughter Susan lives in Spain and calls every week on Sunday nights, visiting in the summer.
Brenda, a neighbour, visits most days and knocks on the wall in the morning to check on Margaret.
Margaret used to attend a lunch club at St Michael's church hall on Thursdays but has not been since the fall due to mobility issues.
She receives a state pension and half of her late husband Frank's railway pension.
She owns the house outright and has approximately nine thousand pounds in savings in the building society.
She disclosed she is not currently receiving Attendance Allowance, though she was informed she might be eligible.
She has a state pension and Frank's pension, from the railway. I get half of it now, a widow's pension.
She has about nine thousand pounds in the building society, which she considers her funeral money and a bit for the grandchildren.
She does not own the house, she rents it.
The social worker will refer Margaret to occupational therapy today for an assessment of the bathroom, stairs, and home environment.
The social worker will make a safeguarding referral regarding the unauthorized withdrawals from Margaret's bank card this afternoon.
The social worker will refer Margaret for a telecare alarm (Careline watch) which will be fitted within about ten days.
The social worker will write to Dr Shah regarding a referral to the falls clinic and will also refer her to the continence service.
The social worker will contact the chemist on Station Road to request a blister pack that is easier for Margaret to open.
The social worker will submit a request for reablement support (morning and teatime visits) and will inform Margaret of the outcome by the end of next week.
The social worker will research transport options for Margaret to attend the lunch club at St Michael's.
Kevin will take Margaret to the Midshire building society branch on Friday morning to cancel her current card and obtain a new one.
Kevin will help Margaret complete the Attendance Allowance form on Sunday.
Kevin will remove the rug from the hall this weekend.
